units.summary: A package declares @jest/test-utils as a dev dependency if and only if some __tests__/tsconfig.json in it references test-utils
units.alint: for_each_dir over packages/* with a nested cross_file set_equals (tsconfig references against the devDependency, read by a layout-dependent regex): jestjs-jest-test-utils-dev-dependency-iff-referenced, jestjs-jest-test-utils-dev-dependency-needs-tests-tsconfig
units.reason: Expressible with for_each_dir plus cross_file set_equals (Stage B, Stage C), but the devDependency side is a regex read of a JSON key restricted to the flat devDependencies object, which is layout-dependent (batch 2 ruling: a regex read of a JSON key is C).

changes.why: Today's kinds express it, so the B-config set label does not hold. Two rules do it. (1) for_each_dir over packages/* with when_iter 'iter.has_file("tsconfig.json") and iter.has_file("package.json") and iter.has_file("**/__tests__/tsconfig.json")', requiring cross_file relation set_equals. Its source.files is '{path}/**/__tests__/tsconfig.json' with extract regex '"path":\s*"[^"]*(test-utils)"' (a unioned set, empty when nothing references test-utils). Its target file is '{path}/package.json' with extract regex '"@jest/(test-utils)":\s*"'. (2) for_each_dir with the same filter but 'not iter.has_file("**/__tests__/tsconfig.json")', requiring json_path_absent $.devDependencies['@jest/test-utils']. Fire-verified on a scratch copy; both rules pass on the copy and on the read-only clone. These breaks fired: devDependency removed from jest-core (whose tsconfigs reference test-utils); jest-core's tsconfig references removed (devDependency kept); devDependency added to jest-mock (no reference); a reference added to jest-mock's __tests__ tsconfig (no devDependency); devDependency added to jest-types (no __tests__ tsconfig), caught by rule 2. Caveat: the package.json regex matches the key in any dependency field, not only devDependencies. jest-10 bans the dependencies field, and peerDependencies and optionalDependencies never carry it. The regex form matches batch-1 trpc-B01, which was A. An integrator who counts regex reads of JSON keys as a tuning should use C.

fields.reason: Expressible with for_each_dir plus cross_file set_equals (Stage B, Stage C), but the devDependency side is a regex read of a JSON key restricted to the flat devDependencies object, which is layout-dependent (batch 2 ruling: a regex read of a JSON key is C).
